title: Cobalt sprint: compact-session-orchestrator mini-PRD fragments
content:
Context / one-line
Cobalt = experimental compact-session orchestrator that runs as a light sidecar (hosted and private) to reduce per-session token costs and enable cheap long-horizon conversations + offline inference reuse. This doc is a collection of fragments for the sprint PRD — rough user stories, hypotheses, acceptance criteria, quick architecture notes and experiment plan.

Why this exists (problem summary)
- Teams building long-lived assistants see token costs explode for long sessions.
- Current approaches (full transcript replay, naive truncation) either lose important context or cost too much.
- We need a pragmatic, low-risk component that sits between request routing and model runtime to compress/transform session state in a manner that keeps useful signals for generation while cutting tokens by ~4-10x for older history.

Primary goals / success metrics (working)
- Reduce average tokens sent to LLM for sessions > 2k tokens by 60%+ without >5% drop in human-rated task success (or degrade gracefully by defined profile).
- Decrease hosted API token bill for targeted cohort by 40% in A/B test (6 week window).
- Latency overhead: <= 50ms p95 extra on request path for cache-hit flows; spinner flows may be longer but < 200ms additional p95.
- Rollout safety: can disable per-customer or per-route; autoswitch to raw transcript mode on quality regressions.

Constraints / non-goals
- Not a replacement for full eval/QA. This is an inference-time optimization, not a fine-tuning or retraining approach.
- Not handling multimodal or large file attachments in first iteration.
- Sidecar must be light-weight, CPU-first prefer; optional optional GPU for heavy embedding ops but baseline should not require GPUs.

Key features (MVP list)
1) Age-based compaction: older segments (beyond N tokens or N turns threshold) get summarized into compact JSON "stubs" that preserve: user intent, important entities, reply history gist, and pointer to canonical embeddings.
2) Semantic deduplication: detect repeated factual statements/boilerplate and collapse them into single compact references.
3) Prefix preservation hook: allow pinned prompts, system messages and last M turns to be sent verbatim (configurable per-route).
4) Fallback & safeties: keep original full transcript in server-side storage for immediate rehydration if user asks to revisit or QA detects hallucination signal.
5) Async offline refresh: a background worker can regenerate compactions when new signals arrive (no blocking on request path).
6) Observability: per-session compression ratio, schema of removed tokens, quick diff preview, quality regressions flagged to console.

User stories (rough)
- As a PM for a conversational product, I want my long-running sessions to cost less so I can scale active users without price changes.
- As an SRE, I want the compactor to be toggleable per-customer and have circuit-breakers for quality rollback.
- As an engineer, I want a simple API to request 'rehydrate(session_id, until_turn=42)' to restore full context for debug paths.
- As a UX researcher, I want a small tool to show what was removed and why (token budget justification) so we can analyze regressions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- End-to-end flow implemented: on incoming request, sidecar returns a compacted context + header describing compression ratio and indicators.
- Default compaction policy (configurable): keep last 6 turns verbatim, compress earlier turns beyond 2k tokens.
- Integration tests proving rehydration returns original transcript and generation responses can be reproduced with rehydrated context.
- Console dashboard tile: per-route avg compression ratio, p95 extra latency, and weekly quality alert counts.
- Feature flag exists for per-customer opt-out; rollout pipeline in console demonstrates toggling.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Compaction format: free-text summary vs structured stubs (entities + intent + condensed messages). Hybrid likely best, but need a canonical schema. Quick thought: one JSON stub per compressed block with fields [summary_text, entities[], salient_user_goals[], embedding_id].
- Where to store rehydration data: ephemeral in sidecar cache (fast) vs durable store (S3) — cost/latency trade-offs. Candidate: keep last 24h in sidecar local cache, archive older to object storage and fetch on-demand.
- Which model to use for summarization/compaction? Use a smaller in-house model (xsmall) for cost; evaluate quality vs using hosted medium model. Also possibility: deterministic heuristics first iteration (rule-based extraction) to minimize model calls.
- How to detect quality regressions automatically? Option: track divergence from baseline via small eval set of prompts per-customer + human-rated sample. Could use perplexity / model confidence heuristics as a cheap proxy.

Mini architecture sketch (notes)
- Request flow (fast path): client -> API Router -> Compact Sidecar (policy apply) -> Serving Runtime. Sidecar returns: compact_context (text + metadata) + compression header.
- Background worker: pulls session deltas, regenerates stubs, computes embeddings, writes to embeddings-store and object storage.
- Cache layers: local LRU memcache per sidecar instance for hot sessions; shared redis for cross-instance pointers; S3 for archival.
- Security: ensure private deployments keep compaction/rehydration data on-customer storage or under KMS. Avoid sending full archive to hosted models unless explicitly allowed.

Experiment plan (first 6 weeks)
Week 0-1: build rule-based compaction prototype (deterministic heuristics) and a tiny dashboard. Run internal load tests.
Week 2-3: implement summarization plug (xsmall model) and sidecar API. Start internal A/B on 10% of internal traffic.
Week 4-6: expand to opt-in beta customers (2-3 teams). Collect qualitative feedback and small human evals. Iterate policy thresholds.

Quick A/B metrics to collect
- Compression ratio distribution (median, p75, p95).
- Per-session token delta (tokens_before - tokens_after).
- Generation quality delta on sampled prompts (human rating change).
- Request path latency delta (p50, p95).
- Billing delta (hosted token spend) for cohort.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: compression removes critical context causing hallucinations. Mitigation: conservative default policy; immediate rehydration on flagged outputs; human-in-loop for first customer rollouts.
- Risk: throughput bottleneck if compaction is synchronous. Mitigation: async compaction + short-circuit heuristics (no compaction for high-priority low-latency routes).
- Risk: storage bloat/complexity. Mitigation: TTL policies, aggregated archiving, customer-configurable retention.

Tasks / next steps (practical)
- [ ] Prototype rule-based compactor (Rowan + Noah) — 1 week.
- [ ] Define minimal stub schema and wire into session-store API (Mika).
- [ ] Small console dashboard tile with compression metrics (Evan).
- [ ] Draft runbook for rollback and rehydration (SRE pairing).
- [ ] Recruit 2 beta customers and prepare opt-in docs and consent language.

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Could allow developer annotations: developers can pin "important" segments to be exempt from compression.
- Consider cheap semantic hashing for de-dup (use local simhash + threshold).
- For private deployments, provide a local-only compaction model binary so data never leaves customer boundary.
- Think about monetization: premium reduction tiers or per-session compression quota for enterprise.

References / inspiration
- Internal: session-pruner experiments (confluence:SESS-1234)
- External: academic work on conversation compression + conversational caching (papers in 2023-24).

End of notes — messy, intentionally. Will refine into proper PRD and tickets after first prototype results.
